column1: In the first half of the 1800s, London’s population grew at an astonishing rate, and the central area became increasingly congested.
column2: 19世纪上半叶，伦敦人口以惊人的速度增长，市中心也日益拥堵。
column5: at an astonishing rate|以惊人的速度

column1: In addition, the expansion of the overground railway network resulted in more and more passengers arriving in the capital.
column2: 此外，地面铁路网不断扩大，乘火车来到首都的旅客也越来越多。

column1: However, in 1846, a Royal Commission decided that the railways should not be allowed to enter the City, the capital’s historic and business centre.
column2: 然而，1846年，一个皇家委员会决定不允许铁路进入伦敦金融城，也就是首都的历史和商业中心。

column1: The result was that the overground railway stations formed a ring around the City.
column2: 结果，地面火车站围绕伦敦金融城形成了一圈。

column1: The area within consisted of poorly built, overcrowded slums and the streets were full of horse-drawn traffic.
column2: 圈内尽是建造粗陋又过度拥挤的贫民区，街上到处是马拉车辆。

column1: Crossing the City became a nightmare.
column2: 横穿伦敦金融城成了一场噩梦。

column1: It could take an hour and a half to travel 8 km by horse-drawn carriage or bus.
column2: 坐马车或公共马车走8公里，有时要花一个半小时。
column3: an hour and a half|一个半小时

column1: Numerous schemes were proposed to resolve these problems, but few succeeded.
column2: 人们提出过许多解决方案，但很少有方案获得成功。

column1: Amongst the most vocal advocates for a solution to London’s traffic problems was Charles Pearson, who worked as a solicitor for the City of London.
column2: 在那些最积极呼吁解决伦敦交通问题的人中，有一位名叫查尔斯·皮尔逊。他当时担任伦敦金融城的事务律师。

column1: He saw both social and economic advantages in building an underground railway that would link the overground railway stations together and clear London slums at the same time.
column2: 他认为，修建一条地下铁路既有社会效益，又有经济效益：它可以把地面各火车站连接起来，同时清除伦敦的贫民区。

column1: His idea was to relocate the poor workers who lived in the inner-city slums to newly constructed suburbs, and to provide cheap rail travel for them to get to work.
column2: 他的想法是，把住在内城贫民区的贫困工人迁往新建的郊区，并提供价格低廉的铁路服务供他们通勤。

column1: Pearson’s ideas gained support amongst some businessmen and in 1851 he submitted a plan to Parliament.
column2: 皮尔逊的想法得到一些商人的支持。1851年，他向议会提交了一项方案。

column1: It was rejected, but coincided with a proposal from another group for an underground connecting line, which Parliament passed.
column2: 这项方案被否决了，但恰在同一时期，另一个团体提出修建一条地下联络线，议会通过了他们的提议。

column1: The two groups merged and established the Metropolitan Railway Company in August 1854.
column2: 这两个团体合并，并于1854年8月成立了大都会铁路公司。
column6: Metropolitan Railway Company|大都会铁路公司

column1: The company’s plan was to construct an underground railway line from the Great Western Railway’s (GWR) station at Paddington to the edge of the City at Farringdon Street — a distance of almost 5 km.
column2: 公司计划修建一条地下铁路线，从大西部铁路公司（GWR）的帕丁顿站通往金融城边缘的法灵顿街，全长将近5公里。
column5: Great Western Railway|大西部铁路公司

column1: The organisation had difficulty in raising the funding for such a radical and expensive scheme, not least because of the critical articles printed by the press.
column2: 为这样一项大胆而昂贵的工程筹款颇为困难，一个重要原因就是报刊上刊出了批评它的文章。
column7: not least because of|一个重要原因是

column1: Objectors argued that the tunnels would collapse under the weight of traffic overhead, buildings would be shaken and passengers would be poisoned by the emissions from the train engines.
column2: 反对者说，隧道会在地面车流的重压下坍塌，楼房会被震动，乘客还会被火车发动机排出的废气毒害。
column5: under the weight of|在……的重压下

column1: However, Pearson and his partners persisted.
column2: 不过，皮尔逊和他的合伙人坚持了下来。

column1: The GWR, aware that the new line would finally enable them to run trains into the heart of the City, invested almost £250,000 in the scheme.
column2: 大西部铁路公司知道，这条新线终将使他们能够把列车开进伦敦金融城的中心，于是向该项目投入了将近25万英镑。

column1: Eventually, over a five-year period, £1m was raised.
column2: 最终，他们在五年间共筹得100万英镑。

column1: The chosen route ran beneath existing main roads to minimise the expense of demolishing buildings.
column2: 选定的路线从现有主干道下方穿过，以便将拆除建筑物的费用降到最低。

column1: Originally scheduled to be completed in 21 months, the construction of the underground line took three years.
column2: 这条地下铁路原定21个月完工，实际修了三年。

column1: It was built just below street level using a technique known as ‘cut and cover’.
column2: 它采用一种叫作“明挖回填法”的技术，修建在紧靠街道地面的下方。

column1: A trench about ten metres wide and six metres deep was dug, and the sides temporarily held up with timber beams.
column2: 工人挖出一条约十米宽、六米深的沟槽，再用木梁临时撑住两侧。

column1: Brick walls were then constructed, and finally a brick arch was added to create a tunnel.
column2: 接着砌起砖墙，最后再加上砖拱，形成一条隧道。

column1: A two-metre-deep layer of soil was laid on top of the tunnel and the road above rebuilt.
column2: 隧道上方铺上两米厚的土层，再重建上面的道路。

column1: The Metropolitan line, which opened on 10 January 1863, was the world’s first underground railway.
column2: 1863年1月10日开通的大都会线，是世界上第一条地下铁路。

column1: On its first day, almost 40,000 passengers were carried between Paddington and Farringdon, the journey taking about 18 minutes.
column2: 开通首日，列车在帕丁顿和法灵顿之间运送了将近四万名乘客，全程约需18分钟。

column1: By the end of the Metropolitan’s first year of operation, 9.5 million journeys had been made.
column2: 到大都会线运营满一年时，累计乘车人次已达950万。
column3: By the end of|到……结束时

column1: Even as the Metropolitan began operation, the first extensions to the line were being authorised; these were built over the next five years, reaching Moorgate in the east of London and Hammersmith in the west.
column2: 大都会线刚开始运营，首批延伸段就已在获批。此后五年间，这些延伸段相继建成，东达伦敦的沼泽门，西抵哈默史密斯。
column6: over the next five years|在接下来的五年间

column1: The original plan was to pull the trains with steam locomotives, using firebricks in the boilers to provide steam, but these engines were never introduced.
column2: 最初的计划是用蒸汽机车牵引列车，借锅炉里的耐火砖产生蒸汽，但这种机车最终并未投入使用。

column1: Instead, the line used specially designed locomotives that were fitted with water tanks in which steam could be condensed.
column2: 这条线路改用了专门设计的机车，上面装有水箱，可以将蒸汽冷凝。

column1: However, smoke and fumes remained a problem, even though ventilation shafts were added to the tunnels.
column2: 不过，尽管隧道加装了通风井，烟雾和废气仍是个问题。

column1: Despite the extension of the underground railway, by the 1880s, congestion on London’s streets had become worse.
column2: 尽管地下铁路有所延伸，到19世纪80年代，伦敦街道的拥堵仍比从前更严重了。

column1: The problem was partly that the existing underground lines formed a circuit around the centre of London and extended to the suburbs, but did not cross the capital’s centre.
column2: 问题部分在于，既有地下线路只在伦敦市中心外围绕行并伸向郊区，却没有横穿首都的中心。

column1: The ‘cut and cover’ method of construction was not an option in this part of the capital.
column2: 在首都这个区域建地铁，明挖回填法行不通。
column5: not an option|不是可行选择

column1: The only alternative was to tunnel deep underground.
column2: 唯一的其他选择，是在地下深处开挖隧道。

column1: Although the technology to create these tunnels existed, steam locomotives could not be used in such a confined space.
column2: 尽管当时已有开挖这类隧道的技术，但蒸汽机车无法在如此封闭的空间里使用。

column1: It wasn’t until the development of a reliable electric motor, and a means of transferring power from the generator to a moving train, that the world’s first deep-level electric railway, the City & South London, became possible.
column2: 直到人们研制出可靠的电动机，并找到把电力从发电机输送到行驶中的列车上的办法，世界第一条深层电气铁路——伦敦金融城与南伦敦铁路——才成为可能。
column9: deep-level electric railway|深层电气铁路

column1: The line opened in 1890, and ran from the City to Stockwell, south of the River Thames.
column2: 这条铁路于1890年开通，从伦敦金融城通往泰晤士河以南的斯托克韦尔。

column1: The trains were made up of three carriages and driven by electric engines.
column2: 每列车由三节车厢组成，由电动机车牵引。

column1: The carriages were narrow and had tiny windows just below the roof because it was thought that passengers would not want to look out at the tunnel walls.
column2: 车厢狭窄，只在紧挨车顶处设有小窗，因为当时人们认为乘客不会想看车外的隧道墙壁。

column1: The line was not without its problems, mainly caused by an unreliable power supply.
column2: 这条线路也有问题，主要是供电不可靠造成的。

column1: Although the City & South London Railway was a great technical achievement, it did not make a profit.
column2: 这条伦敦金融城与南伦敦铁路虽然是了不起的技术成就，却没有盈利。

column1: Then, in 1900, the Central London Railway, known as the ‘Tuppenny Tube’, began operation using new electric locomotives.
column2: 后来，在1900年，人称“两便士地铁”的中央伦敦铁路开始使用新型电力机车运营。
column3: Central London Railway|中央伦敦铁路

column1: It was very popular and soon afterwards new railways and extensions were added to the growing tube network.
column2: 这条铁路很受欢迎，不久之后，新的线路和延伸段也陆续加入了不断扩大的地铁网络。

column1: By 1907, the heart of today’s Underground system was in place.
column2: 到1907年，如今伦敦地铁系统的核心部分已经成形。
